objective: The exit proof's second run (2026-10-30 10:56) had its Codex review refused again as "attempted tools it was denied", with no record of which tripwire fired. Five traced reviews of the same candidate showed why: Codex writes and runs Node scripts that execute the candidate's own validator, and those scripts trip the text tripwires on innocent content (a JavaScript ".." string read as a parent escape; a failed script whose output carried git's own sandbox warning "unable to access '.../.config/git/ignore': Permission denied"). With one added sentence telling the reviewer to review by reading only (git diff/show/log and file reads; no scripts; run no repository code, the loop already ran it), three of three traced reviews ran no script, tripped nothing, and still found the candidate's real defect. Separately, a reviewer REJECT whose findings are all MEDIUM or LOW reaches the gatekeeper as "returned REJECT" with no finding text, so the gatekeeper cannot name a correction. This phase: (1) adds the read-only reviewing sentence to the review instruction; (2) names the reviewer's denial reasons in the refusal; (3) carries a rejection's findings (bounded, inert) into the stop detail when none is CRITICAL or HIGH; (4) ignores git's own config-access warning line when deciding that a failed Codex command was stopped by the sandbox. The exit proof runs after it.
